checks.name: Required Zest packages are declared
checks.command: node -e "const p=require('./package.json');const all=Object.assign({},p.dependencies,p.devDependencies,p.peerDependencies,p.optionalDependencies);const need=['jattac.libs.web.zest-responsive-layout','jattac.libs.web.zest-file-upload','jattac.libs.web.zest-tabs','jattac.libs.web.responsive-table','jattac.libs.web.zest-textbox','jattac.libs.web.zest-sidekick-menu','jattac.libs.web.zest-button','jattac.libs.web.overflow-menu','jattac-web-poller'].filter(n=>n!==p.name);const missing=need.filter(n=>!all[n]);if(missing.length){console.error('Missing required packages: '+missing.join(', '));process.exit(1)}console.log('All required packages are declared.')"

rules.notes: A bespoke component that merely repeats a listed package's function (a custom dropdown instead of jattac.libs.web.overflow-menu, a setInterval poller instead of jattac-web-poller) cannot be recognised by a regular expression and needs review, as does any third-party UI library not named in the import check. Package presence is checked only as a declaration in package.json; jattac.libs.web.zest-sidekick-menu is exempt because this repository is that package, and node_modules installation is not inspected. Native elements spread over several lines or shown in docs/README examples are out of scope.

checks.name: Font sizes scale with user settings
Tablet breakpoint exists
checks.command: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const path=require('path');let css='';for(const d of ['Styles','UI']){if(!fs.existsSync(d))continue;for(const f of fs.readdirSync(d,{recursive:true})){if(f.endsWith('.css'))css+=fs.readFileSync(path.join(d,f),'utf8')}}const m=[...css.matchAll(/@media[^{]*min-width:\s*(\d+)px/g)].map(x=>+x[1]);if(!m.some(n=>n>=600&&n<=1024)){console.error('No tablet-range (600-1024px) min-width breakpoint found');process.exit(1)}console.log('Tablet breakpoint present')"

rules.notes: Whether the UI is genuinely DRY or custom-made for each screen, whether visibility/states adapt meaningfully per device, and whether tablet layouts are actually optimised (rather than merely having a 600-1024px breakpoint) cannot be decided by regexes or commands and needs reviewer judgement. Touch-target checks only cover min-width/min-height declarations, not effective rendered size after transforms or padding.

checks.name: Event listeners are cleaned up
checks.command: node -e "const fs=require('fs'),path=require('path');const exts=['.ts','.tsx'];const bad=[];function walk(d){for(const e of fs.readdirSync(d,{withFileTypes:true})){const p=path.join(d,e.name);if(e.isDirectory())walk(p);else if(exts.includes(path.extname(p))&&!p.includes('.test.')){const s=fs.readFileSync(p,'utf8');const adds=(s.match(/addEventListener\s*\(/g)||[]).length;const rems=(s.match(/removeEventListener\s*\(/g)||[]).length;if(adds>rems)bad.push(p)}}}for(const d of ['UI','utils'])if(fs.existsSync(d))walk(d);if(bad.length){console.error('Event listeners added without matching removeEventListener: '+bad.join(', '));process.exit(1)}console.log('Event listeners are paired with cleanup.')"

rules.notes: Code duplication, general technical debt, algorithmic efficiency, render/memoisation quality, and whether resource usage is actually minimal on a low-spec device cannot be decided by regexes or a shell command and need reviewer judgement. The listener check only compares addEventListener and removeEventListener counts within a single non-test file; it cannot prove cleanup is correct, nor detect leaks from timers, subscriptions, observers, module-level caches or closures, and a deliberate add here/remove there split across files would be flagged. Busy-wait, dynamic-execution and unsafe-HTML checks only cover the literal forms matched by their regexes (aliases, wrappers and multi-line constructions are out of scope), and the JSON deep-clone check flags a shortcut pattern rather than measuring performance.

The rule governs process and git history, not file content: it requires that when code already merged into master is edited additively, characterization tests are created BEFORE the edit. Deciding it needs (a) knowing whether the touched code is merged into master (including via ancestry), (b) judging whether a change is additive vs. intentional behaviour change, and (c) verifying commit/ordering that tests were authored first. A per-line regex cannot decide any of this, and no shell command can reliably distinguish a compliant additive change from a normal refactor without firing on legitimate work. Reviewers must judge this rule from commit history and PR ordering.

Rule USR-005 is recorded only as a heading, "UI/UX, Form Intelligence, and Design System Standards". No requirement, forbidden element, required component/token, measurable limit or standard is stated, so there is nothing an automatic check could enforce: any regex or command would encode rules the owner never gave, and no reviewer has an order to judge against either. The rule needs its actual text (what the design system requires, what form intelligence means here, which standards apply) before checks can be written.

checks.name: Animation honours reduced-motion
checks.command: node -e "const fs=require('fs'),path=require('path');let css='';for(const d of ['Styles','UI']){if(!fs.existsSync(d))continue;for(const f of fs.readdirSync(d,{recursive:true})){if(f.endsWith('.css'))css+=fs.readFileSync(path.join(d,f),'utf8')}}const animates=/(^|[;{\s])(animation|transition)\s*:/.test(css);const guarded=/@media\s*\(prefers-reduced-motion:\s*reduce\)/.test(css);if(animates&&!guarded){console.error('CSS animates but has no prefers-reduced-motion guard');process.exit(1)}console.log('Motion respects prefers-reduced-motion')"

rules.notes: Most of this rule is judged, not matched. Not decidable by regex or command: whether forms order fields logically, focus the right control, validate inline, mark required fields, show useful placeholders/tooltips, auto-populate reliably, and stay usable by keyboard, pointer and touch; whether tooltips are reachable by Tab/Enter on touch and by assistive technology; whether the prediction kernel/adapter split is respected, adapter resolution is predictable, confidence is genuinely calibrated, learning updates correctly ignore invalid entries, and suggestions never overwrite explicit values or interfere with typing or submission; whether the 80%/50% thresholds are applied consistently in real prediction code (no prediction engine exists in this repository, so the shared-kernel logic is unexercised); whether the theme is cohesive and centrally applied beyond colour and font-family placement; and whether the interface is modern, friendly, warm, polished, non-patronising and free of manipulative engagement or gratuitous motion. The reduced-motion command only proves that some prefers-reduced-motion block exists when CSS animates; it cannot verify that every animation and transition is actually covered. Positive tabIndex is treated as the detectable symptom of unpredictable focus order, but focus behaviour itself is not simulated.
